scope: Proposition 7.1 (Fixed-geometry boundary squeeze) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 65. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the domain, signs, a displacement h, the preceding polygonal placements, and a finite list S1, . . . , Sm of allowed plus strips. Let VA ∈ {0, 1}m record their plus crossings in the pure Dobrushin law in an ordinary mesh approximation of Ah. Let V + n record plus crossings in the target, filling the portions of the strips outside Dn virtually with plus. There is a coupling with P(VA ≤ V + n ) = 1 − o(1) (n −→ ∞), (7.3) where the inequality holds coordinatewise. The error is uniform over all admissible target exterior configurations. The sign-reversed construction gives the corresponding transfer of minus crossings from pure domains favoring plus. The smallness condition on λ is the one fixed at the beginning of the section; only the mesh threshold and the error bound depend on these fixed geometries.
